parts.text: Define qualitative and quantitative data using examples.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Design an alternative investigation which tests theory of mind and collects qualitative data.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Evaluate this alternative way of studying theory of mind in methodological and practical terms.

text: Baron-Cohen et al. used the eyes task to collect quantitative data from the participants. An
alternative way to investigate theory of mind would be to collect qualitative data.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What is meant by ecological validity?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why the Mann et al. study has high ecological validity.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of having a study high in ecological validity using the
Mann et al. study as an example.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the extent to which the Mann et al. study has useful applications. 
Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Mann et al. conducted a study to investigate deceptive and truthful behaviour.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the ‘developmental approach’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Freud (little Hans)
Bandura et al. (aggression)
Nelson (children’s morals)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the developmental processes that were investigated in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What problems may psychologists have when they investigate developmental processes in
children?

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘situational explanations of behaviour’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans)
Milgram (obedience)
Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What advantages may psychologists have when they investigate situational explanations of
behaviour?
